title: Finite constant local models
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring with scalar ring $\Lambda(*)$, the ring of
sections over the one-point profinite set, and let $X$ be a scheme. For $U\in X_{\mathrm{proét}}$
there is a ring map from the constant sheaf $\Lambda(*)_U$ to $\Lambda_U$ (adjoint to
$\Lambda(*)\to\Gamma(U,\Lambda_U)$, the pullback along $U\to *$ of global sections). For a
$\Lambda(*)$-module $P$ put $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P:=\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)_U}P_U$.

A $\Lambda_X$-module $M$ has a *finite constant local model* if there are a pro-étale cover
$\{U_i\to X\}$ and finitely presented $\Lambda(*)$-modules $P_i$ with
$M|_{U_i}\simeq\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i$.

**Lemma.** For a $\Lambda_X$-module $M$ and a cover $\{U_i\to X\}$ the following are
equivalent:

1. $M|_{U_i}\simeq\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i$ with $P_i$ finitely presented over
   $\Lambda(*)$;
2. $M|_{U_i}\simeq\operatorname{coker}\bigl(\Lambda_{U_i}^{m_i}\xrightarrow{\ A_i\ }\Lambda_{U_i}^{n_i}\bigr)$
   for a matrix $A_i$ with entries in $\Lambda(*)$, acting through $\Lambda(*)\to\Lambda_{U_i}$.

In particular a module with a finite constant local model is locally finitely presented
([def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]); the converse fails in general, since a local
presentation over $\Lambda_{U}$ may have entries that are not constant.

proof.text: Put $R=\Lambda(*)$. Terminal sections are right adjoint to the sheafified constant functor. Transport braiding across that adjunction, preserving its existing lax monoidal structure, to prove scalarRingObj_comm. The lifted monoidal adjunction makes its counit a monoid morphism, and inverse image preserves this property; monObjObj_comp identifies the successive and composite transported ring structures. Thus scalarCoefficientHom preserves multiplication and unit, and braided constant sheafification followed by inverse image preserves commutativity. The constant-sheaf comparison is the inverse of constantSchemeIso from the module of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant], whose inverse is monoidal. The published upperStarFromPoint and coefficient transport of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] suffice; neither the separate point-pullback specification nor the separate sheaf-tensor specification is used. The constant-sheaf adjunction and inverse unit comparison make pointScalarSection surjective, so every regular condensed-module matrix entry is represented by an ordinary scalar. The composite unit comparison gives precisely scalarSection after inverse image.

proof.text: On $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ set $E_U(P)=\Lambda_U\otimes_{R_U}P_U$. Use the existing module-object categories, their finite-colimit instances and the extension/restriction adjunction [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction]; no conversion to sheaves of modules on a ringed site is required. Mod.isoMk identifies mapMod of the regular module with the regular module. Apply Mod.regularExtensionIso and its naturality from [lem-weil-pbc-regular-extension-comparison] to obtain the extension-of-scalars comparison on regular modules, then Functor.mapBiproduct and biproduct.mapIso for finite free modules. Mod.regular_hom_ext and Mod.one_comp_regularLift verify each matrix entry under that comparison, including the composite monoidal unit. Therefore $E_U(R^k)\cong\Lambda_U^k$ with the actual scalar matrix preserved, rather than merely its ranks.

source.place: first paragraph: the relative tensor and its effect on finite free modules

proof.text: For a finite scalar matrix $A:R^m\to R^n$, put $P=\operatorname{coker}A$. A map $P\to N(U)$ is precisely a map $R^n\to N(U)$ vanishing on $A$. By Step 2 these are precisely the maps $\Lambda_U^n\to N$ vanishing on the sheaf matrix $A$. Consequently $E_U(P)$, with its induced quotient map from $\Lambda_U^n$, has the universal property of $\operatorname{coker}(A:\Lambda_U^m\to\Lambda_U^n)$. This proves the required cokernel identification without any flatness assumption. For $(1)\Rightarrow(2)$ choose the finite scalar presentation of each $P_i$ and apply this calculation with $U=U_i$. For $(2)\Rightarrow(1)$ take $P_i=\operatorname{coker}(A_i:R^{m_i}\to R^{n_i})$; this is finitely presented by definition, and the cokernel universal property just proved identifies $E_{U_i}(P_i)$ with the cokernel in (2), hence with $M|_{U_i}$. Lean implementation: both functors preserve finite colimits and are additive, so PreservesCokernel.iso transports cokernels, and cokernel.mapIso conjugates the presentation through the free-module comparisons. Conversely use the scalar matrix cokernel itself as the finitely presented scalar module. For the comparison with HasFiniteConstantLocalModel, repeat the calculation for mapMod of upperStarFromPoint; surjectivity of pointScalarSection supplies the scalar entries of every condensed finite presentation. This keeps the same cover, including empty covers and zero ranks.

source.place: first and second paragraphs: both implications and the universal-property calculation

proof.text: The matrix presentation in (2) is in particular a cokernel presentation between finite free $\Lambda_{U_i}$-modules, so each restriction is finitely presented. The same given pro-étale cover therefore witnesses local finite presentation by [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. The coefficient identification needed in that definition is $u_i^*\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_{U_i}$ from [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]; to regard a $\Lambda_{U_i}$-action as a $u_i^*\Lambda_X$-action, precompose it with this ring isomorphism, and to reverse the operation precompose with its inverse. These operations are inverse and preserve the regular module, finite direct sums, and cokernel diagrams, so the presentation is one in the module category required by the definition. Lean implementation: map_finitePresentation directly transports the existing finite presentation through mapMod of upperStarFromPoint, so no matrix equivalence is needed here. Restriction along the invertible condensedPullbackHom is an equivalence, and regularIsoOfIsIso, comapCongr, comapComp, comapId and extendScalarsIsoComapInv identify the required underlying pullback module. Transport its finite presentation along this isomorphism.

For the converse take E to be the universe lift of the 2-adic field, S the universe lift of the one-point compactification of the natural numbers, K the universe lift of the rational field, and X=Spec LC(S,K). The locally constant spectrum homeomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum], followed by the unique-point homeomorphism for Spec K, identifies X with S; X is compact and Hausdorff. The continuous function t(n)=2^n and t(infinity)=0 exists by OnePoint.continuousMapMkNat and Padic.norm_p_lt_one. The canonical continuous coefficient realization [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] identifies regular endomorphisms with continuous scalar functions: use the multiplication construction and inverse calculation proved in the module of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-field-matrix-sheaf-normal-form]. Let f be the multiplication endomorphism corresponding to t and M=coker f. The singleton identity cover and the one-by-one regular presentation prove local finite presentation, by [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module] and [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. This replaces the longer route through profinite test objects over an algebraically closed field and coefficient-section localization.

source.place: supplement to the statement final sentence: explicit counterexample (agent argument)

proof.text: For continuous E coefficients, identify the scalar ring with E by evaluating a continuous function on the terminal profinite singleton; verify that the adjunction's lax monoidal sections structure is the pointwise sections structure. Restriction along this ring isomorphism and [lem-weil-pbc-internal-module-ab-equivalence] turn finitely presented scalar modules into finite-dimensional E-vector spaces. Transport a finite basis back to conclude that every finite constant scalar model is finite free. At any point v of a covering member, take an algebraic closure Omega of its residue field and the resulting geometric point a:Spec Omega -> U_i over v. Compose its canonical condensed-module pullback with the additive, finite-colimit-preserving evaluation functor of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-evaluation-functors]. The regular-module normalization identifies its regular coefficient with the continuous scalar at the image of v, by the naturality calculation proved in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-geometric-regular-coefficient]. The extension/restriction isomorphism [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] identifies pullback of the regular module with the regular module, and its composition comparison identifies evaluation of M with evaluation of its local free model. The finite-biproduct coordinates constructed in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-presentation-corank] show that this model has E-dimension n_i. On the other hand, preservation of cokernels reduces this dimension to the cokernel of a one-dimensional endomorphism. If its scalar is zero the dimension is one; if it is nonzero the endomorphism is surjective and the dimension is zero. Thus the function d(x)=1 if t(x)=0 and 0 otherwise is constant, equal to n_i, on each covering member's image. Coordinates are transported explicitly by the evaluation functor applied to the regular-module comparison; functoriality identifies the conjugated scalar. Private generic dimension lemmas separate this computation from the residue-field algebraic closure construction.

source.place: supplement to final sentence: fibres of the counterexample

proof.text: Use the finite affine refinement in the pro-etale covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Each affine member is compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so its continuous image in Hausdorff X is closed. A function constant on each member of a finite closed cover has both closed and open fibres: the fibre of b is the union of images carrying b, and its complement is the union of the other images. Hence d is locally constant. Pulling back along the spectrum homeomorphism gives a locally constant function on the convergent sequence with value zero at every natural number and one at infinity. Its zero fibre, the image of the natural numbers, would be closed. That image is dense and omits infinity (OnePoint.denseRange_coe and OnePoint.infty_notMem_range_coe), a contradiction. This proves failure of the universal converse without changing any quantified statement or excluding empty schemes or zero rings.

source.place: supplement to final sentence: the covering contradiction

proof_origin.place: Three blueprint proof paragraphs formalized through regular-module, finite-biproduct and cokernel comparisons. C9 proves all eight original holes, including the final converse remark by the convergent-sequence 2-adic counterexample, existing continuous realization and geometric evaluation, and a finite closed-cover argument. All auxiliary lemmas are proved privately in the item module; no statement is split off.
